IA No.1 of 2024 for Short Term Bail Application
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, Advocates for the 
applicant.
Mr. S.C. Dumka, A.G.A. for the State.
Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, Senior Advocate 
assisted by Mr. Pavan Kumar Nath, 
Advocate for the informant. 
The applicant seeks short term bail on 
the ground of illness. 
Today, learned State Counsel would 
submit that the applicant’s general 
condition is normal, as per the report, but 
learned counsel for the applicant would 
submit that the applicant is a patient of 
some brain ailments also. He has a clot in 
his brain. He is heavily diabetic. 
As such, investigation reports have
not been placed by learned State Counsel. 
Let State file its response to the short 
term bail application, which is dated 
22.09.2024, enclosing therewith the 
investigation reports and other details of
ailment, if any, with which the applicant is 
suffering. 
Let it be done within two weeks. 
List this matter on 06.11.2024. 
In the meanwhile, the Incharge, Jail, 
is requested to ensure that adequate 
medical facilities are being provided to the 
applicant.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 16.10.2024

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Third Bail Application No. 68 of 2024
Irshad ...Applicant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ...Respondent
Present:-
Mr. Lalit Miglani, Advocate for the applicant.
 Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, A.G.A. for the State.
Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, Senior Advocate, assisted by 
Mr. Prashant Khanna, Advocate for the informant.
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Applicant Irshad is in judicial custody in Case 
Crime No. 422 of 2021, under Section 147, 148, 149, 302, 
307, 323, 504, 506, 120B IPC, Police Station Kotwali 
Laksar, District Haridwar. He has sought short term bail 
on the ground of illness. Initially bail application was filed 
by the applicant, but on 25.09.2024, based on a 
statement given by the learned counsel for the applicant, 
the bail application has been treated as a short term bail 
application.
2. Delay Condonation Application No. 2 of 2024 is 
allowed. Delay in filing the response affidavit is condoned. 
Response affidavit is taken on record. 2
3. Heard learned counsel for the parties and 
perused the record.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would 
submit that the applicant is 61 years old person; he is 
suffering with various ailments including coronary artery 
disease, high diabetic with hypertension.
5. Response was sought from the State. State has 
filed its response. According to it, the applicant is a 
known case of insulin dependent diabetes with 
Hypertension with coronary artery disease with 
diminished vision both eyes. Annexure 1 to the response 
in point no.4 records “Need follow up in AIIMS 
RISHIKESH. Will be sent there on availability of police 
guard.” These lines are not encouraging. If a person needs 
medical assistance, the police guard should be ensured. 
The treatment should not be dependent on the availability 
of police guard. 
6. Learned State counsel would submit that the 
applicant is unwell.
7. Without adverting to the merits, purely on 
humanitarian ground, this Court is of the view that the  3
applicant may be enlarged on short term bail for a 
period of four weeks.
8. Let the applicant be released on short term 
bail for a period of four weeks from the date of his 
release, subject to his furnishing a personal bond and 
two reliable sureties of the like amount, to the 
satisfaction of the court concerned.
9. After expiry of the period of short term bail, 
the applicant shall surrender before the court 
concerned and an information shall be forwarded to this 
Court.
10. Short term bail application is allowed
accordingly.
(Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 13.11.2024
Jitendra

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
MCRC No.03 of 2024 for Time Extension Application
In
BA3 No.68 of 2024
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, Advocate for the 
applicant, through video conferencing.
Mr. V.S. Rawat, A.G.A. for the State.
Applicant was in judicial custody in 
Case Crime No.422 of 2021, under 
Sections 147, 148, 149, 302, 307, 323, 
504, 506 and 120-B IPC, Police Station 
Kotwali Laksar, District Haridwar. He had 
sought short term bail on the ground of 
his illness. Now a Time Extension 
Application, MCRC No.03 of 2024, has 
been filed.
Learned counsel for the applicant 
would submit that the applicant’s one 
finger is to be amputated; the sugar level 
of the applicant is much high; the 
applicant has heart ailments as well.
Yesterday, when the matter was 
taken up, learned State Counsel was 
required to get instructions on the 
medical prescriptions, as filed by the 
applicant. 
Today, learned State Counsel 
confirms that the applicant is unwell and 
he has to undergo surgical procedure. 
Having considered, without adverting 
to the merits, purely on humanitarian 
ground, the Court is of the view that the 
Time Extension Application deserves to be 
allowed.
The Time Extension Application is  allowed. 
The short term bail of the applicant
is further extended to the period of six
weeks from the date of its expiry. It is 
further directed that on expiry of the 
duration of extended short term bail, the 
applicant shall surrender before the court 
concerned and a certificate be produced 
before this Court.
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
13.12.2024
RV
